newsitem.title: UK: Reuters retreats after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Reuters retreats after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Reuters Holdings Plc reversed early gains, after the company warned on Wednesday about the effects of strong sterling on its profits, analysts said.
The share price fell 5-1/2p to 586-1/2p, having touched a day's high of 597p and low of 580-3/4p and having stood 4p higher before the news.
"Everyone knows that sterling has been strong against a basket of currencies but now we're seeing it and now we can see where Reuters' exposure is," said Panmure Gordon analyst Lorna Tilbian.
Panmure is cutting its pre-tax profit forecast for the group to a possible 670-680 million stg for the year from 710 million, she said. Reuters made 701 million stg profit before tax last year.
Another analyst, who declined to be named, said he is keeping his figures at 730 million.
"Traders will see headlines like 'No profits growth in first half' and mark down the price," he said.
"In fact there are no surprises in this and we may see growth in the second half, which will mean overall growth for the whole year," he said.
Oliver Ehrenburg, telecoms analyst at Robert Fleming, a seller of the stock, said the overall figures were as expected but that certain elements were disappointing.
"Growth at Instinet, for example, which grew at 42 percent last year is now growing at nine percent whereas people were expecting 15 percent," he said.
Trading in the stock was brisk with 3.6 million shares changing hands.
